initial_browser.failure: Back to the parent after changing its limit showed cached sections. The per-tab revision had been advanced by refreshing the generated child, so the older parent view was treated as current. Browser1 passed 288 checks before the next wait expired; it exited normally with unchanged hashes and complete clean crash coverage.

validation_sequence: The Firefox 158 oracle confirms four generated query URLs, title sorting after LIMIT, URI sorting before LIMIT, exclusions, queryType and expandQueries. Additional conditions produce empty/error results; removed syntax and unsupported options are recorded separately.
The first host build rejected C++20 string_view helpers under the core C++17 build. The filename parser now uses C++17 operations; all 25 host suites pass.

The first cross-compiled test required explicit JSON string conversions in two comparisons under C++23. This changed test expressions only. Final host and sanitizer sidebar reruns pass; all 12 sanitizer suites pass without diagnostics.
The complete application was built from 351 frozen inputs. The final test-only correction did not change its executable. All 13 native suites pass, including 244 sidebar checks and 120 UI checks.

Browser1 passed the earlier query scenarios and new library rendering, scoped roots, zero-count Downloads, reload, ordinary Back/Forward, real unexpanded native menu activation and parent edit invalidation. Back to the edited parent exposed a stale cached view. The owned browser exited normally, preserving evidence and frozen input hashes.

UpdateBookmarkQueryLocation now invalidates the page revision when a navigation changes the saved query or selected section. Successful internal-page loads revalidate that view; the legacy callback also refreshes its internal page. The application and native probes were rebuilt before the final run.

Browser2 passed the corrected Back/Forward behavior and reached a controller-only root-name lookup error. The lookup was changed to the existing source-root helper; Browser3 uses the same application and focused native binaries.

The final fresh browser repeats the earlier scenarios plus the failed Back case, Forward to the invalidated child, membership restoration, parent deletion, source-specific moves/reimports, HTML round trips and history clearing. Both library pages were visually inspected.

All four selected engine images loaded. Runtime/source hashes remained unchanged, normal shutdown left no helpers, and the complete crash interval contained no debugger events. An all-team scan preceded removal of the owned RAMFS.
limits: This does not complete #110: new Summit navigation/download classification, Chrome transition mapping, annotations, frecency, visit parent restrictions, complex grouped conditions and full matching semantics remain unfinished.

The library Downloads query matches retained imported Firefox visit types. History retains the existing 2000-page and timestamp sampling bounds. History and Tags use Summit retained data; All Bookmarks resolves the library source roots.
Unsupported library conditions and options show explanations. Type7 is the deprecated tag-contents view and remains unsupported.
Runtime acceptance uses isolated modern airOS x86_64 and the unchanged accepted engine. It does not establish stock-Haiku runtime, legacy-WebKit runtime, ARM, or Framework Teams/Zoom acceptance.
